title: Analyzing the Limits of Self-Supervision in Handling Bias in Language
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the ability of self-supervised language models to perform four tasks related to bias: diagnosis (detecting presence of bias), identification (labeling the specific dimension of bias, such as 'Religion'), extraction (identifying the biased span), and rephrasing (removing the bias). Religion is one of the specific bias dimensions tested under the 'Identity-directed Abuse' category using the Contextual Abuse Dataset (CAD).
findings: The study found significant disparities in the models' ability to identify different dimensions of bias. Specifically, GPT-Neo performed poorly in identifying bias related to 'Religion' in zero-shot settings (0-13.3% accuracy depending on the prompt type), which was significantly lower than its performance on 'Political Affiliation' (58.9-75.1%) and 'Gender' (4.8-19.6%). While providing few-shot examples improved performance for religion bias identification (up to ~32% with Question-type prompts), it generally remained lower than other categories, indicating a skew in the model's internal representation of different biases.
